blocks.title: Phylum - Chordata
blocks.text:
Fundamentally characterised by :-

  • A notochord - Mesodermal, dorsal to gut.
  • A nerve cord - Single, hollow and dorsal.
  • Paired pharyngeal gill slits.

rows: Central nervous system is dorsal, hollow and single.
Central nervous system is ventral, solid and double.

blocks.title: Phylum – Chordata is divided into three sub phylum
blocks.text:
1. Sub Phylum – Urochordata or Tunicata:
(Exclusively marine)

Notochord - In larval tail only.
Examples : Ascidia, Salpa, Doliolum

2. Sub Phylum - Cephalochordata:
Notochord extends from head to tail region and persist through out their life.
Examples : Branchiostoma (Amphioxus or Lancelet)

3. Sub Phylum Vertebrata:
Posses notochord during the embryonic period
The notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult.
Thus all vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.
Beside the basic chordate characters, Vertebrates have
    • A ventral muscular heart with two, three or four chambers.
    • Kidney for excretion and osmoregulation.
    • Paired appendages (may be fins or limbs)

blocks.title: Class-Cyclostomata
blocks.text:
• All are ectoparasite on some fishes.
    • 6-15 pairs of gill-slits.
    • Sucking and circular mouth without jaw.
    • Body devoid of scales and paired fins.
    • Cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous.
    • Cyclostomes are marine but migrate for spawning to fresh water  spawning  after  within few days they die.
    • Their larvae, after metamorphosis, return to ocean.

Examples: Petromyzon (Lamprey), Myxine (Hag fish)

blocks.title: Class-Chondrichthyes
blocks.text:
• Cartilaginous endoskeleton

• Ventrally mouth

• Notochord is persistent throughout life

• 5-7 pairs of gill slits are separate and without operculum.

• Powerful jaw (predaceous)

• Electric organs (Torpedo)

• Poison sting (Trygon)

• The skin is tough, containing minute placoid scales.

• Teeth are modified placoid scales which are backwardly directed.

• Due to the absence of air bladder, they have to swim constantly to avoid sinking.

• They are cold blooded or poikilothermic.

• Examples: Scoliodon (Dog fish), Pristis (Saw fish), Carcharodon (Great white shark), Trygon (Sting ray), Torpedo (Electric ray).

blocks.title: Class-Osteichthyes
blocks.text:
• Their body is streamlined.

• Mouth terminal.

• 4-Pairs of gills covered by operculum on each side.

• Skin is covered with cycloid/ctenoid scales.

• Air bladder is present which regulates buoyancy.

• They are cold blooded or poikilothermic animals.

Examples:

Marine - Exocoetus (Flying fish), Hippocampus (Sea horse);

Freshwater - Labeo (Rohu), Catla (Katla), Clarias (Magur);

Aquarium - Betta (Fighting fish), Pterophyllum (Angel fish).

blocks.title: Class - Amphibia
blocks.text:
• Amphibian can live in aquatic as well as terrestrial habitats.
    • Most of them have two pairs of limbs.
    • Body divisible into head and trunk, Tail may present in some.
    • Skin is Moist (without scales)
    • Eyes have eyelids
    • Tympanum represents ear.
    • Cloaca present.
    • Sexes are separate.
    • They are cold blooded or poikilothermic animals.

Examples : Bufo (Toad), Rana (Frog), Hyla (Tree frog), Salamandra (Salamander), Ichthyophis (Limbless amphibia).

blocks.title: Class - Reptilia
blocks.text:
• Creeping or crawling mode of locomotion.
    • Dry and cornified skin support terrestrial habitats.
    • Epidermal scales or scutes.
    • Tympanum represents ear.
    • Snakes and lizards shed their scales as skin cast.
    • Limbs, when present are two pairs (absent in snakes)
    • They are cold blooded or poikilothermic animals.
    • Sexes are separate.

Examples : Chelone (Turtle), Testudo (Tortoise), Chameleon (Tree lizard), Calotes (Garden lizard), Crocodilus (Crocodile), Alligator (Alligator).

Hemidactylus (Wall lizard), Poisonous snakes - Naja (Cobra), Bangarus (Krait), Vipera (Viper).

blocks.title: Class - Aves
blocks.text:
• Characteristic features - Presence of feathers.
    • Skin-Dry without gland. [Except-Oil gland at the base of tail]
    • Pneumatic (hollow) bone.
    • Air sacs connected to lungs supplement respiration.
    • Most of them can fly except flightless birds (e.g. Ostrich)
    • The fore limbs are modified into wings.
    • The hind limbs generally have scales and are modified for walking, swimming or clasping the tree branches.
    • The digestive tract of birds has additional chambers, the crop and gizzard.
    • They are warm blooded or homoiothermous.
    • Sexes are separate.

Examples : Corvus (Crow), Columba (Pigeon), Psittacula (Parrot), Struthio (Ostrich), Pavo (Peacock), Aptenodytes (Penguin), Neophron (Vulture).

blocks.title: Class - Mammalia
blocks.text:
• Characteristic - Presence of milk producing glands (mammary glands) - (Most unique character)
    • Skin - Possessing hair.
    • External ear or Ear pinnae present.
    • Mostly viviparous.
    • They have two pairs of limbs, adapted for walking, running climbing, burrowing, swimming or flying.
    • They are warm blooded or homoiothermous.

Examples : Oviparous-Ornithorhynchus (Platypus); Viviparous Macropus (Kangaroo), Pteropus (Flying fox), Camelus (Camel), Macaca (Monkey), Rattus (Rat), Canis (Dog), Felis (Cat), Elephas (Elephant), Equus (Horse), Delphinus (Common dolphin), Balaenoptera (Blue whale), Panthera tigris (Tiger), Panthera leo (Lion).

blocks.title: Class-Cyclostomata
blocks.text:
• All are ectoparasite on some fishes.
    • 6-15 pairs of gill-slits.
    • Sucking and circular mouth without jaw.
    • Body devoid of scales and paired fins.
    • Cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous.
    • Cyclostomes are marine but migrate for spawning to fresh water  spawning  after  within few days they die.
    • Their larvae, after metamorphosis, return to ocean.

Examples: Petromyzon (Lamprey), Myxine (Hag fish)

blocks.title: Class-Osteichthyes
blocks.text:
• Their body is streamlined.

• Mouth terminal.

• 4-Pairs of gills covered by operculum on each side.

• Skin is covered with cycloid/ctenoid scales.

• Air bladder is present which regulates buoyancy.

• They are cold blooded or poikilothermic animals.

Examples:

Marine - Exocoetus (Flying fish), Hippocampus (Sea horse);

Freshwater - Labeo (Rohu), Catla (Katla), Clarias (Magur);

Aquarium - Betta (Fighting fish), Pterophyllum (Angel fish).

blocks.title: Class - Amphibia
blocks.text:
• Amphibian can live in aquatic as well as terrestrial habitats.
    • Most of them have two pairs of limbs.
    • Body divisible into head and trunk, Tail may present in some.
    • Skin is Moist (without scales)
    • Eyes have eyelids
    • Tympanum represents ear.
    • Cloaca present.
    • Sexes are separate.
    • They are cold blooded or poikilothermic animals.

Examples : Bufo (Toad), Rana (Frog), Hyla (Tree frog), Salamandra (Salamander), Ichthyophis (Limbless amphibia).

blocks.title: Class - Reptilia
blocks.text:
• Creeping or crawling mode of locomotion.
    • Dry and cornified skin support terrestrial habitats.
    • Epidermal scales or scutes.
    • Tympanum represents ear.
    • Snakes and lizards shed their scales as skin cast.
    • Limbs, when present are two pairs (absent in snakes)
    • They are cold blooded or poikilothermic animals.
    • Sexes are separate.

Examples : Chelone (Turtle), Testudo (Tortoise), Chameleon (Tree lizard), Calotes (Garden lizard), Crocodilus (Crocodile), Alligator (Alligator).

Hemidactylus (Wall lizard), Poisonous snakes - Naja (Cobra), Bangarus (Krait), Vipera (Viper).

blocks.title: Class - Aves
blocks.text:
• Characteristic features - Presence of feathers.
    • Skin-Dry without gland. [Except-Oil gland at the base of tail]
    • Pneumatic (hollow) bone.
    • Air sacs connected to lungs supplement respiration.
    • Most of them can fly except flightless birds (e.g. Ostrich)
    • The fore limbs are modified into wings.
    • The hind limbs generally have scales and are modified for walking, swimming or clasping the tree branches.
    • The digestive tract of birds has additional chambers, the crop and gizzard.
    • They are warm blooded or homoiothermous.
    • Sexes are separate.

Examples : Corvus (Crow), Columba (Pigeon), Psittacula (Parrot), Struthio (Ostrich), Pavo (Peacock), Aptenodytes (Penguin), Neophron (Vulture).

blocks.title: Class - Mammalia
blocks.text:
• Characteristic - Presence of milk producing glands (mammary glands) - (Most unique character)
    • Skin - Possessing hair.
    • External ear or Ear pinnae present.
    • Mostly viviparous.
    • They have two pairs of limbs, adapted for walking, running climbing, burrowing, swimming or flying.
    • They are warm blooded or homoiothermous.

Examples : Oviparous-Ornithorhynchus (Platypus); Viviparous Macropus (Kangaroo), Pteropus (Flying fox), Camelus (Camel), Macaca (Monkey), Rattus (Rat), Canis (Dog), Felis (Cat), Elephas (Elephant), Equus (Horse), Delphinus (Common dolphin), Balaenoptera (Blue whale), Panthera tigris (Tiger), Panthera leo (Lion).

rows: Central nervous system is dorsal, hollow and single.
Central nervous system is ventral, solid and double.
